title.zh: 卷一百七十四 列傳第六十一: 姚燧 郭貫 夾谷之奇 劉賡 耶律有尚 郝天挺 張孔孫
title.en: Volume 174 Biographies 61: Yao Sui, Guo Guan, Jia Guzhiqi, Liu Geng, Ye Luyoushang, Hao Tianting, Zhang Kongsun
title.raw: 卷一百七十四 列傳第六十一: 姚燧 郭貫 夾谷之奇 劉賡 耶律有尚 郝天挺 張孔孫 Volume 174 Biographies 61: Yao Sui, Guo Guan, Jia Guzhiqi, Liu Geng, Ye Luyoushang, Hao Tianting, Zhang Kongsun

sentences.zh: 姚燧，字端甫，世系見燧伯父樞傳。

translations.literal: Yao Sui, styled Duanduanfu; his lineage is recorded in the biography of his uncle Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Sui, whose style was Duanduanfu, came of a family whose line is set out in the biography of his uncle Yao Shu.

sentences.zh: 父格。

translations.literal: His father was Ge.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Ge.

sentences.zh: 燧生三歲而孤，育於伯父樞。

translations.literal: Sui lost his father at age three and was raised by his uncle Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Sui was orphaned at three and was brought up by his uncle Shu.

sentences.zh: 樞隱居蘇門，謂燧蒙暗，教督之甚急，燧不能堪。

translations.literal: Shu lived in seclusion at Sumen, considered Sui dull and ignorant, and pressed his instruction very urgently; Sui could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had retired to Sumen, judged Sui slow-witted, and drove his lessons hard; Sui found it unbearable.

sentences.zh: 楊奐馳書止之曰：「燧，令器也，長自有成爾，何以急為！

translations.literal: Yang Huan sent a hurried letter to stop him, saying: "Sui is fine material; when grown he will achieve on his own—why be so urgent!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huan wrote in haste to restrain him: "Sui is promising timber; in time he will ripen on his own—why such haste!"

sentences.zh: 」且許醮以女。

translations.literal: " Moreover he promised to betroth his daughter to him.
translations.idiomatic: " He also pledged his daughter in marriage to Sui.

sentences.zh: 年十三，見許衡於蘇門。

translations.literal: At thirteen he met Xu Heng at Sumen.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he met Xu Heng at Sumen.

sentences.zh: 十八，始受學於長安。

translations.literal: At eighteen he first received instruction in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he began formal study in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 時未嘗為文，視流輩所作，惟見其不如古人，則心弗是也。

translations.literal: At the time he had never yet written; when he looked at what his contemporaries produced, he only saw that it fell short of the ancients, and in his heart he did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: He had not yet tried his hand at writing; reading what his peers wrote, he found only that it did not measure up to the ancients, and he inwardly rejected it.

sentences.zh: 二十四，始讀韓退之文，試習為之，人謂有作者風。

translations.literal: At twenty-four he first read the writings of Han Tuizhi, tried practicing them, and people said he had the manner of a master author.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-four he first read Han Yu's prose, practiced imitating it, and others said he already showed a master's touch.

sentences.zh: 稍就正於衡，衡亦賞其辭，且戒之曰：「弓矢為物，以待盜也；

translations.literal: He gradually sought correction from Heng; Heng also admired his compositions, yet admonished him, saying: "Bows and arrows are things made to await robbers;
translations.idiomatic: He gradually submitted his drafts to Xu Heng, who admired his style but warned him: "Bows and arrows exist to meet robbers;

sentences.zh: 使盜得之，亦將待人。

translations.literal: if robbers obtain them, they too will await men."
translations.idiomatic: if robbers seize them, they too will wait upon men."

sentences.zh: 文章固發聞士子之利器，然先有能一世之名，將何以應人之見役者哉！

translations.literal: Literary composition is indeed the sharp weapon by which scholar-gentlemen make their names heard, yet if one first gains a reputation able to dominate an age, how will one answer those who see and employ one!
translations.idiomatic: Writing is indeed the scholar's weapon for making a name, but if you win a reputation that towers over your age first, how will you answer everyone who comes to put you to use!"

sentences.zh: 非其人而與之，與非其人而拒之，鈞罪也，非周身斯世之道也。

translations.literal: To give it to one who is not the right person and to refuse one who is not the right person are equal faults—not the way to preserve oneself through this world."
translations.idiomatic: Giving your work to the wrong man and refusing the right one are the same fault; neither is how to keep your footing in this world."

sentences.zh: 」至元七年，衡以國子祭酒教貴冑，奏召舊弟子十二人，燧自太原驛致館下。

translations.literal: " In the seventh year of Zhiyuan, Heng as Director of the Imperial Academy instructed the noble scions; he memorialized to summon twelve former disciples, and Sui came from the Taiyuan post station to lodge below the academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan (1270), as director of the Imperial Academy Xu Heng taught the imperial clansmen; he memorialized to recall twelve former pupils, and Sui traveled from the Taiyuan courier station to join them at the academy.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，仁宗居籓邸，開宮師府，燧年已七十，遣正字呂洙，如漢徵四皓故事，起燧為太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida, Renzong resided at the princely residence and opened a palace tutors' office; Sui was already seventy; he sent Proofreader Lü Zhu, following the Han story of summoning the Four Hoary Heads, to raise Sui as Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhida (1308), while Renzong still held his princely establishment, he opened a tutors' bureau. Sui was already seventy; Renzong sent proofreader Lü Zhu, in the manner of the Han summons of the Four White-Heads of Shangshan, to bring Sui out of retirement as guest of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除承旨學士，尋拜太子少傅。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Academician Expositor-in-Chief; soon after he was invested as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made expositor-in-chief academician, and soon after junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 武宗面諭燧，燧拜辭，謝曰：「昔臣先伯父樞嘗除是官，尚不敢拜，臣何敢受！

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong personally instructed Sui; Sui bowed and declined, apologizing: "Formerly my late uncle Shu was once appointed to this office and still did not dare accept the investiture—how dare I receive it!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong addressed him in person; Sui bowed and declined, saying, "My late uncle Shu was once offered this post and even he did not dare accept it—how could I?"

sentences.zh: 」明年，授榮祿大夫、翰林學士承旨、知制誥兼修國史。

translations.literal: " The next year he was granted Grand Master of Glorious Blessings, Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief, Controller of Imperial Drafts, and concurrent Compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he received the rank of grand master of glorious blessings, with the posts of Hanlin expositor-in-chief, controller of imperial drafts, and concurrent compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 四年，得告南歸，中書以承旨召；

translations.literal: In the fourth year he obtained leave and returned south; the Central Secretariat summoned him as expositor-in-chief;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he took leave and went home to the south; the Central Secretariat summoned him back as expositor-in-chief;

sentences.zh: 明年，復召。

translations.literal: the next year he was summoned again.
translations.idiomatic: the next year they summoned him again.

sentences.zh: 燧以病，俱不赴。

translations.literal: Sui pleaded illness and on both occasions did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Both times Sui pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 卒於家，年七十六。

translations.literal: He died at home, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Wen (Cultured).

sentences.zh: 燧先在蘇門山時，讀《通鑑綱目》，嘗病國統散於逐年，不能一覽而得其離合之概，至告病江東，著《國統離合表》若干卷，年經而國緯之，如《史記》諸《表》，將附硃熹《凡例》之後，復取徽、建​​二本校仇，得三誤焉，序於《表》首。

translations.literal: When Sui was earlier on Mount Sumen he read the Comprehensive Mirror in Outline; he once took as a fault that dynastic legitimacy was scattered year by year, so that one could not survey it at a glance and grasp the outline of its separations and unions. When he took sick leave in Jiangdong he composed several scrolls of Tables of the Separation and Union of Legitimacies, threading years and weaving states, like the various Tables in the Records of the Grand Historian, intending to append them after Zhu Xi's General Principles; he then collated the Huizhou and Jian editions and found three errors, which he set out in a preface at the head of the Tables.
translations.idiomatic: While living on Mount Sumen, Sui had read Zhu Xi's Outline of the Comprehensive Mirror and disliked how legitimacy was scattered year by year so that one could not see at a glance how regimes split and reunited. On sick leave in Jiangdong he wrote several scrolls of Tables on the Separation and Union of Legitimacies, arranging years as warp threads and states as weft, in the manner of Sima Qian's tables, to append after Zhu Xi's General Principles. Collating the Huizhou and Jian editions, he found three errors and prefaced the tables with his findings.

sentences.zh: 略曰：「其一，建安二十五年，徽本作『延康元年』。

translations.literal: In summary he said: "First, in the twenty-fifth year of Jian'an, the Huizhou edition reads 'first year of Yan'kang.'"
translations.idiomatic: In brief he wrote: "First: for Jian'an 25 the Huizhou text reads 'first year of Yan'kang.'"

sentences.zh: 《凡例》：中歲改元，在興廢存亡之際，以前為正。

translations.literal: The General Principles: when the reign title is changed mid-year, at the juncture of rise, fall, survival, and extinction, the earlier title is taken as correct.
translations.idiomatic: The General Principles state that when a reign title changes mid-year, at the moment of a dynasty's rise or fall the earlier title should prevail.

sentences.zh: 當從建本，於建安二十五年下，注『改元延康』。

translations.literal: One should follow the Jian edition and under the twenty-fifth year of Jian'an note 'reign title changed to Yan'kang.'"
translations.idiomatic: The Jian edition is correct: under Jian'an 25 one should note 'reign title changed to Yan'kang.'"

sentences.zh: 其二，章武三年，徽本大書『三年，後主禪建興元年』，建本無『三年』，則昭烈為無終。

translations.literal: Second, in the third year of Zhangwu the Huizhou edition writes large characters 'third year; the Later Lord abdicated, first year of Jianxing,' while the Jian edition lacks 'third year,' so that Emperor Zhaolie would have no conclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Second: for Zhangwu 3 the Huizhou text prominently reads 'year 3; the Later Lord abdicated, Jianxing year 1,' but the Jian text omits 'year 3,' which would leave Emperor Zhaolie without a closing year.

sentences.zh: 徽、建皆曰『後主』，於君臣父子之教，所害甚大，是起十四卷、盡十六卷，凡曰後主者，皆失於刊正也。

translations.literal: Both Huizhou and Jian say 'Later Lord,' which greatly harms the teaching of ruler and minister, father and son—from scroll fourteen through scroll sixteen, wherever it says Later Lord, all are failures of editorial correction.
translations.idiomatic: Both editions call him 'Later Lord,' which gravely offends the norms of ruler and subject, father and son. From scroll 14 through 16, every instance of 'Later Lord' is an editorial lapse.

sentences.zh: 當於三年下注『帝禪建興元年』，明年大書『帝禪建興二年』，庶前後無齟齬也。

translations.literal: One should under the third year note 'the Emperor abdicated, first year of Jianxing,' and the next year write large 'the Emperor abdicated, second year of Jianxing,' so that before and after there is no contradiction.
translations.idiomatic: Under year 3 one should note 'the emperor abdicated, Jianxing year 1,' and the next year headline 'the emperor abdicated, Jianxing year 2,' so the sequence does not clash.

sentences.zh: 其三，天寶十五載注『肅宗皇帝至德元載』，明年惟曰『二載』，為無始。

translations.literal: Third, in the fifteenth year of Tianbao a note reads 'Emperor Suzong, first year of Zhide'; the next year it only says 'second year,' so there is no beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Third: Tianbao 15 carries a note 'Emperor Suzong, Zhide year 1,' but the next entry reads only 'year 2,' leaving Zhide without a proper opening.

sentences.zh: 當大書『二載』上加『肅宗皇帝至德』，使上同於開元。

translations.literal: One should write large above 'second year' 'Emperor Suzong, Zhide,' so that it matches above with Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Year 2 should be headed 'Emperor Suzong, Zhide year 2,' matching how Kaiyuan is treated above.

sentences.zh: 三者鈞失，而建安之取，至德之去，統固在也。

translations.literal: All three are equal errors, yet in taking Jian'an and removing Zhide, legitimacy itself remains.
translations.idiomatic: All three are editorial slips, yet whether one adopts Jian'an or drops Zhide, the thread of legitimacy still holds.

sentences.zh: 若章武之距建興，才三年耳，遽有帝父主子之異，豈不於統大有關乎！

translations.literal: If from Zhangwu to Jianxing is only three years, yet suddenly there is the difference of emperor, father, and lord and subject—is this not greatly related to legitimacy!
translations.idiomatic: From Zhangwu to Jianxing is only three years, yet the text suddenly shifts from 'emperor' to 'father' and 'lord'—surely that bears on how legitimacy is read!

sentences.zh: 」詳見《序篇》。

translations.literal: " The details are in the Preface.
translations.idiomatic: " See the preface for the full argument.

sentences.zh: 燧之學，有得於許衡，由窮理致知，反躬實踐，為世名儒。

translations.literal: Sui's learning had its gain from Xu Heng; through investigating principle to extend knowledge and turning back upon oneself in real practice, he became a renowned Confucian of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's scholarship owed much to Xu Heng: he pursued principle to knowledge and tested it in his own conduct, and was acclaimed as a leading Confucian of his day.

sentences.zh: 為文閎肆該洽，豪而不宕，剛而不厲，舂容盛大，有西漢風，宋末弊習，為之一變。

translations.literal: In writing he was broad and comprehensive, magnificent without excess, forceful without harshness, ample and grand in tone, with the manner of the Western Han; the decadent habits of late Song were thereby transformed.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was expansive and learned, bold without extravagance, firm without harshness, flowing and ample in the Western Han manner, and it broke the late-Song mannerisms.

sentences.zh: 蓋自延祐以前，文章大匠，莫能先之。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, before the Yanyou era, among great masters of letters none could take precedence over him.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Yanyou period (1314–1320), no master of letters ranked above him.

sentences.zh: 或謂世無知燧者，曰：「豈惟知之，讀而能句，句而得其意者，猶寡。

translations.literal: Some said the age did not know Sui; he said: "It is not only that they know—those who can read and parse, parse and grasp the meaning, are still few."
translations.idiomatic: When someone said the world did not appreciate Sui, he replied, "They know me well enough; readers who can parse my lines and grasp their meaning are still rare."

sentences.zh: 」燧曰：「世固有厭空桑而思聞鼓缶者乎，然文章以道輕重，道以文章輕重。

translations.literal: " Sui said: "Surely in the world there are those who tire of the empty mulberry yet wish to hear the sounding of clay drums; yet writing is weighed by the Way, and the Way is weighed by writing."
translations.idiomatic: Sui added, "Surely some in the world tire of plain zither yet long to hear clay drums; still, writing is judged by the Way, and the Way by writing."

sentences.zh: 彼復有班孟堅者出，表古今人物，九品中必以一等置歐陽子，則為去聖賢也有級而不遠，其文雖無謝、尹之知，不害於行後。

translations.literal: If again a Ban Mengjian should appear, tabulating men ancient and modern, he would surely place Master Ouyang in the first rank of the nine grades—then in departing from the sages and worthies there would be gradation yet not distance; though his writing lacked the understanding of Xie and Yin, it would not harm his standing after death.
translations.idiomatic: If another Ban Gu should rank men past and present, he would place Master Ouyang in the top grade of the nine ranks—close to the sages yet not confused with them. Though his prose lacked the discernment of Xie Lingyun and Yin Zhongrong, it would not keep him from enduring renown.

sentences.zh: 豈有一言幾乎古，而不聞之將來乎！

translations.literal: How could there be a single word approaching the ancients that would not be heard in the future!
translations.idiomatic: Can words that nearly match the ancients fail to reach posterity!"

sentences.zh: 」當時孝子順孫，欲發揮其先德，必得燧文始可傳信；

translations.literal: " At the time filial sons and obedient grandsons who wished to display their forebears' virtue had to obtain Sui's writing before it could be transmitted as credible;
translations.idiomatic: In his day filial sons and grandsons who wished to commemorate their ancestors' virtue needed a text by Sui before the record could be trusted;

sentences.zh: 其不得者，每為愧恥。

translations.literal: those who could not obtain it were each time ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: those who failed to secure one often felt ashamed.

sentences.zh: 故三十年間，國朝名臣世勳、顯行盛德，皆燧所書。

translations.literal: Therefore for thirty years the dynasty's famous ministers, hereditary merit, illustrious conduct, and abundant virtue were all written by Sui.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years the memorial inscriptions of the dynasty's great ministers, hereditary worthies, and men of eminent virtue were almost all his work.

sentences.zh: 每來謁文，必其行業可嘉，然後許可，辭無溢美。

translations.literal: Whenever men came requesting compositions, their conduct and achievements had to be praiseworthy before he would consent; his wording had no excess praise.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted commissions only when the subject's conduct deserved praise, and he never flattered in his wording.

sentences.zh: 又稍廣置燕樂，燧則為之喜而援筆大書，否則弗易得也。

translations.literal: If they also somewhat broadly provided banquet music, Sui would be pleased and take up the brush to write large characters; otherwise it was not easily obtained.
translations.idiomatic: If they also laid on a generous feast with music, he would be pleased and write boldly; otherwise his brush was hard to obtain.

sentences.zh: 時高麗瀋陽王父子，連姻帝室，傾貲結朝臣。

translations.literal: At the time the king of Korea at Shenyang and his son, allied by marriage to the imperial house, poured out wealth to bind court officials.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Shenyang in Goryeo and his son, both related to the imperial clan by marriage, spent lavishly to win over courtiers.

sentences.zh: 一日，欲求燧詩文，燧靳不與，至奉旨，乃與之。

translations.literal: One day they wished to obtain Sui's poetry and prose; Sui was stingy and would not give them; only when an imperial order was received did he finally grant them.
translations.idiomatic: One day they asked for his poetry and prose; he refused until an imperial command compelled him to comply.

sentences.zh: 王贈謝幣帛、金玉、名畫五十篚，盛陳致燧。

translations.literal: The king presented thanks of silks, gold and jade, and famous paintings in fifty baskets, lavishly displayed and sent to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: The king sent fifty baskets of silk, gold, jade, and famous paintings as thanks, arrayed before Sui.

sentences.zh: 燧即分散諸屬官及史胥侍從，止留金銀，付翰林院為公用器皿，燧一無所取。

translations.literal: Sui at once distributed them among subordinate officials and clerks, attendants, and followers; he kept only gold and silver, handed to the Hanlin Academy as communal vessels, and Sui took nothing for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sui immediately distributed the gifts among his staff and attendants, kept only the gold and silver for the Hanlin Academy's common use, and took nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 人問之，燧曰：「彼籓邦小國，唯以貨利為重，吾能輕之，使知大朝不以是為意」。

translations.literal: When people asked him, Sui said: "That is a small border state; they value only goods and profit—I can treat it lightly and let them know the great court does not regard such things as important."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Sui said, "They are a small tributary state that cares only for profit; by treating their gifts lightly I show that the great court does not prize such things."

sentences.zh: 其器識豪邁過人類如此。

translations.literal: His breadth of vision and bold spirit surpassing others were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the breadth and boldness of his character.

sentences.zh: 然頗恃才，輕視趙孟頫、元明善輩，故君子以是少之。

translations.literal: Yet he rather relied on his talent and looked down on Zhao Mengfu, Yuan Mingshan, and their like; therefore gentlemen for this reason thought somewhat less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he leaned on his talent and slighted Zhao Mengfu, Yuan Mingshan, and others, which is why men of discernment held him somewhat lower for it.

sentences.zh: 平生所著，有《牧庵文集》五十卷行於世。

translations.literal: What he wrote in his lifetime included the Collected Works of Muan in fifty scrolls circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His lifetime writings include the fifty-scroll Collected Works of Muan, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子三：塤，圻，城。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Xun, Qi, and Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Xun, Qi, and Cheng.

sentences.zh: 郭貫，字安道，保定人。

translations.literal: Guo Guan, styled Andao, was a man of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Guan, whose style was Andao, was from Baoding.

sentences.zh: 以才行見推擇，為樞密中書掾，調南康路經歷，擢廣西道提刑按察司判官，會例格，授濟南路經歷。

translations.literal: For ability and conduct he was seen and selected, made a clerk of the Privy Council and Central Secretariat, transferred as Administrator of Nankang Circuit, promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Guangxi Circuit Surveillance Commission for Punishment and Investigation; meeting a regulation barrier, he was appointed Administrator of Jinan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for ability and conduct, he served as a clerk in the Privy Council and Central Secretariat, then as administrator of Nankang Circuit, and was promoted to vice commissioner of the Guangxi surveillance commission; when regulations blocked further promotion, he was appointed administrator of Jinan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 至元二十七年，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Zhiyuan (1290) he was appointed supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 承詔分江北沿淮草地，劾淮西宣慰使昂吉兒父子專權，久不遷調，蠹政害民。

translations.literal: He received an edict to divide the pasturelands along the Huai north of the river in Jiangbei; he impeached Angir, Pacification Commissioner of Huai West, and his son for monopolizing power, long without transfer or reassignment, corrupting government and harming the people.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial orders he surveyed pasturelands along the Huai in northern Jiangbei and impeached Angir, the Huai West pacification commissioner, and his son for monopolizing power, remaining in post too long, and harming the people through corrupt rule.

sentences.zh: 三十年，僉湖南肅政廉訪司事。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was appointed Concurrent Commissioner of the Hunan Commission for Upholding Governance and Investigating Corruption.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1293) he became concurrent commissioner of the Hunan integrity and surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 大德初，遷湖北道，言「今四省軍馬，以數万計，徵八百媳婦國，深入為炎瘴萬里不毛之地，無益於國。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dade he was transferred to Hubei Circuit and said: "Today the armies of the four provinces number in the tens of thousands; campaigning against the Eight Hundred Wives' Kingdom, penetrating deep into a region of miasma and fever across ten thousand li of barren land, is of no benefit to the state."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dade era (1297–1307) he moved to the Hubei commission and said, "The four provinces now field armies numbering in the tens of thousands. The campaign against the Eight Hundred Wives' Kingdom sends them deep into malarial wastes a thousand li across—of no benefit to the state."

sentences.zh: 」五年，遷江西道，賑恤饑民，有惠政，入為御史臺都事。

translations.literal: " In the fifth year he was transferred to Jiangxi Circuit, relieved and comforted famine victims, had benevolent policies, and entered the capital as Director of Affairs of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1301) he was transferred to Jiangxi, where he relieved famine victims with effective relief policies, then entered the capital as director of affairs in the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷集賢待制，進翰林直學士，奉詔與遼陽行省平章政事別速台徹里帖木兒往鎮高麗。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Attendant-in-Waiting of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, advanced to Direct Academician of the Hanlin, and by imperial order went with Biesutai Cher Temür, Pacification Commissioner of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, to garrison Korea.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1304) he became attendant-in-waiting at the Hall of Gathered Worthies and was promoted to direct Hanlin academician; by imperial order he joined Biesutai Cher Temür, pacification commissioner of Liaoyang, to oversee Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 十一年，召為河東廉訪副使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was summoned as Vice Commissioner of the Hedong Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1307) he was recalled as vice commissioner of the Hedong integrity commission.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，仁宗至五台山，貫進見，仁宗因問：「廉訪使滅里吉歹何以有善政？

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida, Renzong arrived at Mount Wutai; Guan presented himself; Renzong thereupon asked: "How did Surveillance Commissioner Mielijidai come to have good policies?"
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhida (1309), when Renzong visited Mount Wutai, Guan was presented to him. Renzong asked, "How did surveillance commissioner Mielijidai achieve such good government?"

sentences.zh: 」左右對曰：「皆副使郭貫之教也。

translations.literal: " Those at his side answered: "It is all the instruction of Vice Commissioner Guo Guan."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants replied, "It was all the teaching of Vice Commissioner Guo Guan."

sentences.zh: 」因賜貫瑪瑙數珠、金織文幣，入為吏部考功郎，遂拜治書侍御史。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he bestowed on Guan agate prayer beads and gold-woven patterned silks; Guan entered as Evaluator of Merit in the Ministry of Personnel, and then was appointed Associate Censor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong then gave Guan agate prayer beads and gold-woven silks, brought him into the Ministry of Personnel as evaluator of merit, and soon appointed him associate censor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年，除禮部尚書，帝親書其官階曰嘉議大夫，以授有司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Minister of Rites; the Emperor personally wrote his official rank as Grand Master for Discussion of Policy and handed it to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1311) he was appointed minister of rites; the emperor personally wrote his rank as grand master for discussion of policy and handed the document to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，擢淮西廉訪使，尋留不遣，改侍御史，俄遷翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Huai West; soon he was retained and not sent out, changed to Attending Censor, and shortly transferred to Hanlin Academician Explaining the Classics.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangqing (1312) he was promoted to Huai West surveillance commissioner, but was kept at court, made attending censor, and soon Hanlin lecturer.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為淮西廉訪使。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as Surveillance Commissioner of Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was sent out as Huai West surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 建言「宜置常平倉，考校各路農事」。

translations.literal: He proposed: "Constant-level granaries should be established and agriculture in each circuit examined and verified."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed establishing ever-normal granaries and auditing agricultural affairs in every circuit.

sentences.zh: 延祐二年，召拜中書參知政事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanyou he was summoned and appointed Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yanyou (1315) he was recalled and made associate administrator of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，升左丞，加集賢大學士。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Left Chancellor and added as Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was promoted to left chancellor and given the additional title of grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 五年，除太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1318) he was appointed grand mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 貫​​言：「皇太子受金寶已三年，宜行冊禮；

translations.literal: Guan said: "The Heir Apparent has received the gold seal and treasures for three years; the investiture ceremony should be performed;
translations.idiomatic: Guan said, "The heir apparent has held the golden seal and regalia for three years; the formal investiture should be carried out;

sentences.zh: 又，輔導之官，早宜選置。

translations.literal: furthermore, the officials to guide and assist him should early be selected and appointed."
translations.idiomatic: and tutors to guide him should be chosen without delay."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " His advice was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 六年，加太子賓客，謁告還家。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was added as Guest of the Heir Apparent, requested leave, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1319) he was also made guest of the heir apparent, took leave, and went home.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，復起為集賢大學士，尋致仕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi he was again raised as Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies; soon he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhizhi (1321) he was recalled as grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, but soon retired.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，遷翰林學士承旨，不起。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding he was transferred to Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiding (1324) he was offered Hanlin expositor-in-chief but declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 至順二年，以疾卒，年八十有二。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhishun he died of illness, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhishun (1331) he died of illness at eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿大夫、河南行省平章政事、柱國，追封蔡國公，諡文憲。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Blessings, Pacification Commissioner of the Henan Branch Secretariat, and Pillar of the State; enfeoffed as Duke of Cai, with posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he received the ranks of grand master of splendid blessings, pacification commissioner of Henan, and pillar of the state; was enfeoffed as Duke of Cai with the posthumous title Wenxian (Cultured and Law-abiding).

sentences.zh: 貫​​博學，精於篆籀，當世冊寶碑額，多出其手云。

translations.literal: Guan was broadly learned and skilled in seal and large-seal script; the age's edicts, treasures, and stele inscriptions mostly came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was broadly learned and excelled in seal script; most of the dynasty's edicts, imperial treasures, and stele headings were said to be his work.

sentences.zh: 夾谷之奇

translations.literal: Jia Guzhiqi
translations.idiomatic: Jia Guzhiqi

sentences.zh: 夾谷之奇，字士常，其先出女真加古部，後訛為夾谷，由馬紀嶺撒曷水徙家於滕州。

translations.literal: Jia Guzhiqi, styled Shichang; his ancestors came from the Jurchen Jiagu tribe, later corrupted to Jiagu; from Sahashui on Majiling they moved their household to Tengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Guzhiqi, whose style was Shichang, was descended from the Jurchen Jiagu tribe, later written as Jiagu; his family moved from Sahashui on Majiling to settle in Tengzhou.

sentences.zh: 之奇少孤，舅杜氏攜之至東平，因受業於康曄。

translations.literal: Zhiqi was orphaned young; his maternal uncle the Du clan brought him to Dongping, where he received instruction from Kang Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was taken by his uncle's Du family to Dongping, where he studied under Kang Ye.

sentences.zh: 授濟寧教授，辟中書省掾。

translations.literal: He was appointed Instructor of Jining and recruited as a clerk of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as instructor at Jining and was recruited as a Central Secretariat clerk.

sentences.zh: 大兵南伐宋，授行省左右司都事。

translations.literal: When the great army campaigned south against Song, he was appointed Director of Affairs of the Left and Right Bureaus of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the southern campaign against Song he was appointed director of affairs in the branch secretariat's left and right bureaus.

sentences.zh: 時行省官與中書權臣有隙，特遣使核其財用，而之奇職文書，亦被按問。

translations.literal: At the time the branch secretariat officials had a rift with powerful ministers of the Central Secretariat; a special envoy was dispatched to audit their finances, and Zhiqi, whose duty was documents, was also investigated.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat had fallen out with powerful Central Secretariat ministers, who sent an envoy to audit its accounts; Zhiqi, who handled documents, was questioned as well.

sentences.zh: 張弘範率其屬詣使者言：「夾谷都事素公清，若少有侵漁，弘範當與連坐。

translations.literal: Zhang Hongfan led his subordinates to the envoy and said: "Director Jia has always been upright and clean; if he has the slightest embezzlement, Hongfan should share the punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hongfan went with his staff to the envoy and said, "Director Jia has always been upright; if he has taken so much as a penny, I should share his punishment."

sentences.zh: 」會御史臺立，擢之奇僉江南浙西道提刑按察司事，既而移僉江北淮東。

translations.literal: " At this time the Censorate was established; Zhiqi was promoted to Concurrent Commissioner of the Jiangnan and Zhexi Circuit Surveillance Commission for Punishment and Investigation, and later transferred to concurrent commissioner of Jiangbei and Huaidong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Censorate was established, he was made concurrent commissioner of the Jiangnan and Zhexi surveillance commission, then transferred to the Jiangbei and Huaidong commission.

sentences.zh: 至元十九年，召為吏部郎中，立陟降澄汰之法，著為令式。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan he was summoned as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, established methods for promotion, demotion, clarification, and elimination, and set them down as regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan (1282) he was recalled as director in the Ministry of Personnel, drew up rules for promotion, demotion, and purging of officials, and codified them as statutes.

sentences.zh: 歲大旱，有司議平穀價，以遏騰湧之患。

translations.literal: That year there was great drought; the responsible offices discussed stabilizing grain prices to check the harm of soaring prices.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of severe drought the authorities proposed fixing grain prices to curb inflation.

sentences.zh: 之奇言：「莫若省經費，輟土木之役，庶足召和氣，弭災變，而有豐稔之期。

translations.literal: Zhiqi said: "Nothing is better than reducing expenditures and suspending earth-and-wood works; perhaps that is enough to summon harmonious qi, quell calamitous changes, and bring the prospect of abundant harvest."
translations.idiomatic: Zhiqi said, "Better to cut spending and halt construction projects; that may restore harmony, end the disaster, and bring a good harvest."

sentences.zh: 」二十一年，遷左贊善大夫。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-first year he was transferred to Left Supporter of Goodness Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year (1284) he was made left supporter of goodness.

sentences.zh: 時裕宗為皇太子，每進見，必賜坐，顧遇甚優。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Yu was heir apparent; whenever Zhiqi came to audience he was always granted a seat; his treatment was very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu was then heir apparent; whenever Zhiqi attended audience he was given a seat and treated with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 權臣有欲以均輸法益國賦者，慮提刑按察司撓其事，請令與轉運司並為一職，詔集群臣議之。

translations.literal: A powerful minister wished to use the equalizing transport law to increase state revenue; fearing the Surveillance Commission for Punishment and Investigation would obstruct the matter, he requested that it be merged with the Transport Commission into one office; an edict gathered the ministers to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: A powerful minister sought to increase revenue through the equalizing transport system and, fearing the surveillance commission would block it, asked that it be merged with the transport commission; the emperor ordered a ministerial debate.

sentences.zh: 之奇言：「按察司者，控制諸路，發擿姦伏，責任匪輕。

translations.literal: Zhiqi said: "The Surveillance Commission controls the circuits, exposes hidden wrongdoing, and its responsibility is not light.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiqi said, "The surveillance commission oversees the circuits and uncovers hidden wrongdoing—a weighty charge.

sentences.zh: 若使理財，則心勞事冗，將彌縫自救之不暇，又安能繩糾他人哉！

translations.literal: If made to manage finances, the mind would be weary and affairs numerous; one would have no leisure to patch and save oneself, so how could one bind and correct others!
translations.idiomatic: If charged with revenue as well, one would be too busy covering one's own tracks to discipline anyone else!"

sentences.zh: 並之弗便。

translations.literal: Merging them would not be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Merging the two offices would not work.

sentences.zh: 」事遂寢。

translations.literal: " The matter was then laid to rest.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 又與諭德李謙條具時政十事，上之皇太子：一曰正心，二曰睦親，三曰崇儉，四曰幾諫，五曰戢兵，六曰親賢，七曰革敝，八曰尚文，九曰定律，十曰正名。

translations.literal: He also, with Instructor Li Qian, itemized ten matters of current policy and presented them to the Heir Apparent: first, rectifying the mind; second, harmonizing kin; third, honoring frugality; fourth, subtle remonstrance; fifth, restraining arms; sixth, drawing near the worthy; seventh, reforming abuses; eighth, esteeming culture; ninth, establishing laws; tenth, rectifying names.
translations.idiomatic: With instructor Li Qian he drew up ten policy recommendations for the heir apparent: rectify the mind; harmonize kin; honor frugality; remonstrate subtly; restrain arms; draw near the worthy; reform abuses; esteem culture; establish laws; and rectify names.

sentences.zh: 會皇太子薨，除翰林直學士，改吏部侍郎，遂拜侍御史。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent died, he was appointed Direct Academician of the Hanlin, changed to Vice Minister of Personnel, and then invested as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent died, he was made direct Hanlin academician, then vice minister of personnel, and soon attending censor.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，丁母憂，以吏部尚書起復，屢請終制，不許。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he mourned his mother; he was recalled from mourning as Minister of Personnel; he repeatedly requested to complete the mourning period and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he entered mourning for his mother; recalled as minister of personnel before the mourning term ended, he repeatedly asked to finish the full period but was refused.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 之奇慮識精審，明於大體，而不忽細微，為政卓卓可稱，雖老於吏學者，自以為不及。

translations.literal: Zhiqi's deliberation and insight were precise and careful; he was clear on great principles yet did not neglect minute details; in government he was outstanding and praiseworthy—even veterans of clerkly learning considered themselves his inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiqi thought carefully and grasped the large picture without neglecting detail; his governance was notably effective, and even seasoned administrators admitted they could not match him.

sentences.zh: 為文章尤簡嚴有法，多傳於世云。

translations.literal: In writing he was especially concise, strict, and methodical; much was transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was especially concise and disciplined, and much of it circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 劉賡，字熙載，洺水人。

translations.literal: Liu Geng, styled Xizai, was a man of Moshui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Geng, whose style was Xizai, was from Moshui.

sentences.zh: 五世祖逸，以郡吏治獄，有陰德。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Yi, as a commandery clerk handling cases, had hidden virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Yi, as a commandery clerk in charge of trials, performed hidden acts of virtue.

sentences.zh: 祖肅，為左三部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Su was Minister of the Left Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Su served as minister of the left three departments.

sentences.zh: 賡幼有文名，師事翰林學士王磐。

translations.literal: Geng in youth had a literary reputation and took Wang Pan, Hanlin Academician, as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Geng was known for literary talent from youth and studied under Hanlin academician Wang Pan.

sentences.zh: 至元十三年，用薦者授國史院編修官。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan, on recommendation he was appointed Compiler of the National History Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan (1276) he was recommended and appointed compiler at the National History Academy.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to Hanlin Attendant for Imperial Composition.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year (1279) he became Hanlin attendant for imperial composition.

sentences.zh: 辟為司徒府長史，仍兼應奉。

translations.literal: He was recruited as Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education's office while still concurrently serving as Attendant for Composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited as chief clerk of the minister of education's office while retaining his Hanlin attendant post.

sentences.zh: 補外，同知德州事，考滿，擢太廟署丞、太常博士，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He filled an outside post as Associate Administrator of Dezhou; when his evaluation term ended he was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Office and Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Posted outside the capital as associate administrator of Dezhou, he was promoted after his term to vice director of the imperial ancestral temple office and erudite of the imperial ancestral temple, then appointed supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 是時，御史中丞崔彧好盛氣待人，他御史拜謁，或平受之，獨見賡，則待以上客。

translations.literal: At this time Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu liked to treat others with overbearing spirit; when other censors came to pay respects he sometimes received them levelly, but when he saw Geng alone he treated him as a honored guest.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Cui Yu was overbearing toward others; when other censors called he sometimes received them casually, but he always treated Geng as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 大德二年，升翰林直學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade he was promoted to Direct Academician of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dade (1298) he was promoted to direct Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 六年，奉使宣撫陝西。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was sent on mission as Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1302) he was dispatched to pacify and oversee Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 由侍講學士升學士。

translations.literal: From Academician Explaining the Classics he was promoted to Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Hanlin lecturer to full academician.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，遷禮部尚書，仍兼翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida he was transferred to Minister of Rites while still concurrently Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhida (1309) he became minister of rites while retaining his Hanlin academician title.

sentences.zh: 尋拜侍御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made attending censor.

sentences.zh: 頃之，還翰林為學士承旨，兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Shortly he returned to the Hanlin as Academician Expositor-in-Chief and concurrently Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned to the Hanlin as expositor-in-chief and concurrent director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 國學故事，伴讀生以次出補吏，莫不爭先出。

translations.literal: By precedent of the National Academy, companion-reading students were released in order to fill official posts, and none failed to vie to go out first.
translations.idiomatic: By academy custom, companion readers were released in seniority order to take official posts, and all rushed to go first.

sentences.zh: 時有一生，親老且貧，同舍生有名在前者，因博士以告曰：「我齒頗少，請讓之先。

translations.literal: At the time one student had aged parents and was poor; a dormitory mate whose name ranked ahead, through the erudite, reported: "I am rather junior in standing—please let him go first."
translations.idiomatic: One student had aged, impoverished parents; a roommate ranked ahead asked the erudite, "I am junior in standing—please let him go out first."

sentences.zh: 」賡曰：「讓，德之恭也。

translations.literal: " Geng said: "Yielding is the reverence of virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Geng said, "Yielding is the reverence of virtue."

sentences.zh: 」從其讓，別為書薦其人，朝廷反先用之。

translations.literal: " He followed the yielding, separately wrote a letter recommending that man, and the court in fact used him first.
translations.idiomatic: He granted the request, wrote a separate recommendation for the student who had yielded, and the court in fact appointed him first.

sentences.zh: 自是六館之士，皆知讓之為美德也。

translations.literal: From this the students of the six lodges all knew yielding as a beautiful virtue.
translations.idiomatic: From then on students in all six lodges understood yielding as a virtue.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，遷集賢大學士，仍兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was transferred to Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies while still concurrently Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangqing (1312) he became grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies while still directing the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，復為承旨；

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he was again made expositor-in-chief;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanyou (1314) he again became expositor-in-chief;

sentences.zh: 六年，拜太子賓客；

translations.literal: in the sixth year he was appointed Guest of the Heir Apparent;
translations.idiomatic: in the sixth year (1319) he was made guest of the heir apparent;

sentences.zh: 七年，復入集賢為大學士；

translations.literal: in the seventh year he again entered the Hall of Gathered Worthies as Grand Academician;
translations.idiomatic: in the seventh year (1320) he returned to the Hall of Gathered Worthies as grand academician;

sentences.zh: 尋又入翰林為承旨。

translations.literal: soon he again entered the Hanlin as expositor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: and soon after rejoined the Hanlin as expositor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding he was given the additional rank of Grand Master of Splendid Blessings.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiding (1324) he received the additional rank of grand master of splendid blessings.

sentences.zh: 會集議上尊號，賡獨抗言其不可，事遂已。

translations.literal: When there was a joint conference to bestow an honorific title, Geng alone spoke against it as improper, and the matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated an honorific title for the emperor, Geng alone objected, and the proposal was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 天曆元年卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianli he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Tianli (1328) at eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 賡久典文翰，當時大製作多出其手，以耆年宿德，為朝廷所推重云。

translations.literal: Geng long directed literary composition; at the time great works mostly came from his hand; as an aged man of longstanding virtue, he was esteemed by the court.
translations.idiomatic: Geng long oversaw the literary bureau, and most major compositions of the age came from his hand; as an elder of established virtue, the court held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 耶律有尚

translations.literal: Ye Luyoushang
translations.idiomatic: Ye Luyoushang

sentences.zh: 耶律有尚，字伯強，遼東丹王十世孫。

translations.literal: Ye Luyoushang, styled Boqiang, was tenth-generation descendant of the King of Eastern Dan of Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Luyoushang, whose style was Boqiang, was a tenth-generation descendant of the Liao king of Eastern Dan.

sentences.zh: 祖父在金世嘗官於東平，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather in the Jin age had once held office at Dongping and therefore made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather had served in Dongping under the Jin and settled his family there.

sentences.zh: 有尚資識絕人，篤志於學，受業許衡之門，號稱高第弟子。

translations.literal: Youshang's native intelligence surpassed others; he was devoted in will to learning, received instruction in Xu Heng's school, and was acclaimed a top-ranking disciple.
translations.idiomatic: Youshang's talent was exceptional; devoted to learning, he studied under Xu Heng and was counted among his foremost pupils.

sentences.zh: 其學邃於性理，而尤以誠為本，儀容辭令，動中規矩，識與不識，莫不服其為有道之君子。

translations.literal: His learning was profound in nature and principle, yet especially took sincerity as root; in bearing, speech, and command his movements always hit the rule—whether they knew him or not, none failed to submit that he was a gentleman possessed of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: His learning went deep into moral principle, with sincerity as its foundation; in bearing and speech he always observed propriety, and all who met him, friend or stranger, acknowledged him as a true gentleman.

sentences.zh: 至元八年，衡罷中書左丞，除集賢大學士，兼國子祭酒，以教國人之子弟，乃奏以門人十二人為齋長以伴讀，有尚其一也。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan, Heng was dismissed as Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat and appointed Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, concurrently Director of the Imperial Academy, to teach the sons of the state's people; he memorialized to make twelve disciples lodge heads as companion readers—Youshang was one.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan (1271), after Xu Heng left the left chancellorship, he became grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and director of the Imperial Academy to teach the sons of the ruling families. He memorialized to appoint twelve disciples as lodge heads and companion readers; Youshang was among them.

sentences.zh: 十年，衡告免還鄉里，朝廷乃以有尚等為助教，嗣領其學事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Heng requested leave and returned to his home district; the court then made Youshang and others Assistant Instructors to succeed in leading his academic affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1273) Xu Heng retired to his home district; the court appointed Youshang and others assistant instructors to carry on his teaching.

sentences.zh: 居久之，拜監察御史，不赴。

translations.literal: After residing long in the post, he was appointed Supervising Censor but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was offered the post of supervising censor but declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 除秘書監丞，出知薊州，為政以寬簡得民情。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Library, went out as Prefect of Jizhou, and in government by leniency and simplicity won the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the Imperial Library, then sent out as prefect of Jizhou, where lenient, simple governance won popular affection.

sentences.zh: 裕宗在東宮，召為詹事院長史。

translations.literal: When Prince Yu was in the Eastern Palace, he was summoned as Chief Clerk of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu held the eastern palace, Youshang was summoned as chief clerk of the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 自有尚既去，而國學事頗廢，廷議以謂非有尚無足以繼衡者，除國子司業。

translations.literal: After Youshang had left, the affairs of the National Academy were rather neglected; court discussion held that without Youshang none could suffice to succeed Heng, and he was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After Youshang left, academy affairs declined; the court concluded that only he could succeed Xu Heng, and appointed him vice director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 時學館未建，師弟子皆寓居民屋，有尚屢以為言。

translations.literal: At the time the academy buildings were not yet built; teachers and students all lodged in private houses; Youshang repeatedly spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: The academy buildings had not yet been built, and teachers and students lodged in private homes; Youshang raised the matter repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，朝廷乃大起學舍，始立國子監，立監官，而增廣弟子員。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the court then greatly raised academy buildings, first established the Directorate of the Imperial Academy, set directorate offices, and expanded the number of student places.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year (1287) the court built academy halls on a large scale, established the Imperial Academy directorate with its officers, and expanded enrollment.

sentences.zh: 於是有尚升國子祭酒，儒風為之丕振。

translations.literal: Thereupon Youshang was promoted to Director of the Imperial Academy, and Confucian style was thereby greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: Youshang was then promoted to director of the Imperial Academy, and Confucian learning flourished again.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，以親老，辭職歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, because his parents were aged, he resigned his post and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year (1290) he resigned and went home to care for his aged parents.

sentences.zh: 大德改元，復召為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: At the change of reign title to Dade he was again summoned as Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dade era began (1297) he was again summoned as director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 尋除集賢學士，兼其職。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, concurrently holding that post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies while retaining the directorship.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷太常卿，又遷集賢學士。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Minister of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, then again transferred to Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he became minister of the imperial ancestral temple, then returned to the Hall of Gathered Worthies as academician.

sentences.zh: 八年，葬父還鄉里。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he buried his father and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1304) he buried his father and returned home.

sentences.zh: 已而朝廷思用老儒，以安車召之於家，累辭不允，復起為昭文館大學士，兼國子祭酒，階中奉大夫。

translations.literal: Before long the court wished to employ aged Confucians; with a comfort carriage he was summoned to his home; he repeatedly declined and was not permitted; he was raised again as Grand Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Literature, concurrently Director of the Imperial Academy, rank Grand Master for Court Audience.
translations.idiomatic: The court then wished to employ veteran Confucians and summoned him from home in a comfort carriage; though he declined repeatedly, he was obliged to return as grand academician of the Hall of Brilliant Literature and director of the Imperial Academy, with the rank of grand master for court audience.

sentences.zh: 有尚前後五居國學，其立​​教以義理為本，而省察必真切；

translations.literal: Youshang five times in all held the National Academy; in establishing teaching he took moral principle as root, and in self-examination he was always genuine;
translations.idiomatic: Youshang headed the Imperial Academy five times in all. He grounded instruction in moral principle and demanded genuine self-examination;

sentences.zh: 以恭敬為先，而踐履必端愨。

translations.literal: he put reverence first, and in practice was always upright and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: he put reverence first and insisted on upright conduct in practice.

sentences.zh: 凡文詞之小技，綴緝雕刻，足以破裂聖人之大道者，皆屏黜之。

translations.literal: All petty skills of literary phrasing, patchwork carving and polish sufficient to rupture the sages' great Way, were all screened out and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed petty literary ornament that could fracture the sages' great Way.

sentences.zh: 是以諸生知趨正學，崇正道，以經術為尊，以躬行為務，悉為成德達材之士。

translations.literal: Therefore the students knew to hasten toward correct learning, honor the correct Way, take classical studies as honored, and take personal practice as task—all became men of completed virtue and accomplished talent.
translations.idiomatic: Students therefore pursued orthodox learning, honored the true Way, esteemed the classics, and practiced what they taught, producing men of full virtue and real ability.

sentences.zh: 大抵其教法一遵衡之舊，而勤謹有加焉。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, his teaching method wholly followed Heng's old practice, yet with added diligence and care.
translations.idiomatic: His method followed Xu Heng's precedent, with even greater diligence.

sentences.zh: 身為學者師表者數十年，海內宗之，猶如昔之宗衡也。

translations.literal: His person as model for scholars lasted several decades; within the seas he was revered, just as in former times Heng was revered.
translations.idiomatic: For decades he was the scholars' model; the empire revered him as it had once revered Xu Heng.

sentences.zh: 有尚既以年老，力請還家，朝廷复頒楮幣七千緡，即其家賜之。

translations.literal: When Youshang, already aged, strenuously requested to return home, the court again issued seven thousand strings of paper currency and bestowed them at his home.
translations.idiomatic: When age led him to press for retirement, the court sent seven thousand strings of paper money to his home as a gift.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十六，賜諡文正。

translations.literal: He died aged eighty-six; he was granted the posthumous title Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-six and was given the posthumous title Wenzheng (Cultured and Upright).

sentences.zh: 郝天挺

translations.literal: Hao Tianting
translations.idiomatic: Hao Tianting

sentences.zh: 郝天挺，字繼先，出於朵魯別族，自曾祖而上，居安肅州。

translations.literal: Hao Tianting, styled Jixian, came from the Dorben tribe; from his great-grandfather upward they dwelt in Ansu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Tianting, whose style was Jixian, came from the Dorben tribe; from his great-grandfather's generation the family lived in Ansu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父和上拔都魯，太宗、憲宗之世多著武功，為河東行省五路軍民萬戶。

translations.literal: His father Heshang Badulu in the ages of Taizong and Xianzong achieved many military feats and was Ten-Thousand-Household of the Five Circuits' Military and Civil Affairs of the Hedong Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Heshang Badulu won distinction in the reigns of Taizong and Xianzong and became ten-thousand-household over military and civil affairs of the five circuits in the Hedong branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天挺英爽剛直，有志略，受業於遺山元好問，以勳臣子，世祖召見，嘉其容止，有旨：宜任以政，俾執文字，備宿衛春宮。

translations.literal: Tianting was spirited, bright, and uprightly firm, with will and strategy; he received instruction from Yishan Yuan Haowen; as son of a meritorious minister, Shizu summoned him, praised his bearing and demeanor, and issued an order: he should be entrusted with government, made to handle documents, and prepared as palace guard of the Spring Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Tianting was spirited, upright, and ambitious; he studied under Yuan Haowen of Yishan. As the son of a meritorious minister, he was summoned by Shizu, who admired his bearing and ordered that he enter government, handle documents, and serve in the heir apparent's guard.

sentences.zh: 裕宗遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: Prince Yu treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu treated him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 建省雲南，選官屬，遂除參議雲南行尚書省事，尋升參知政事，又擢陝西漢中道廉訪使。

translations.literal: When the Yunnan province was established and officials were selected, he was appointed Counselor of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat, soon promoted to Associate Administrator, and again elevated to Surveillance Commissioner of the Shaanxi Hanzhong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunnan province was established he was chosen as counselor of the Yunnan branch secretariat, soon promoted to associate administrator, then surveillance commissioner of the Shaanxi Hanzhong circuit.

sentences.zh: 未幾，入為吏部尚書，尋除陝西行御史臺中丞，又遷四川行省參政及江浙行省左丞，俱不赴。

translations.literal: Before long he entered as Minister of Personnel; soon he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate, then transferred to Administrator of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat and Left Chancellor of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat—all of which he did not take up.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered the capital as minister of personnel, then was offered vice censor-in-chief of Shaanxi, administrator of Sichuan, and left chancellor of Jiangzhe—but declined each post.

sentences.zh: 拜中書左丞，與宰相論事，有不合，輒面斥之。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat; when discussing affairs with the chief minister, if they did not agree he would at once rebuke him to his face.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed left chancellor of the Central Secretariat, he openly rebuked the chief minister whenever they disagreed.

sentences.zh: 一日，以奏事敷陳明允，特賜黃金百兩，不受。

translations.literal: One day, because in memorializing affairs he laid them out clearly and fairly, he was specially granted one hundred taels of gold, which he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor rewarded his clear, fair memorials with a gift of one hundred taels of gold, which he refused.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「非利汝也，第旌汝肯言耳。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "This is not to profit you—it is only to commend your willingness to speak."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This is not for your profit—only to honor your willingness to speak plainly."

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，仁宗以太后命，首定大難，及武宗還自朔方，遂入正大統，定策之際，天挺與有力焉。

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, Renzong by the Empress Dowager's order first settled the great crisis; when Wuzong returned from the northern frontier he then entered the true succession; at the time of fixing the policy Tianting had forceful part.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengzong's death Renzong, acting on the empress dowager's orders, first resolved the succession crisis; when Wuzong returned from the north and took the throne, Tianting had played a decisive role.

sentences.zh: 仁宗臨御，收召故老天挺與少保張閭等十人，共議大政，革尚書省之弊，遂成皇慶之治。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne he gathered aged worthies—Tianting and Junior Guardian Zhang Lü and nine others—to deliberate on great policy, reform the abuses of the Secretariat, and thereby achieve the governance of Huangqing.
translations.idiomatic: On taking the throne Renzong recalled veteran statesmen—Tianting, junior guardian Zhang Lü, and eight others—to reform Secretariat abuses and establish the Huangqing order.

sentences.zh: 又出為江西、河南二省右丞，召拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: He again went out as Right Chancellor of Jiangxi and Henan provinces and was summoned and appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as right chancellor in Jiangxi and Henan, then was recalled as vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 入見，首陳紀綱之要，以獵為喻曰：「御史職在擊姦，猶鷹揚焉，禽之，弱者易獲也，其力大者，必借人力。

translations.literal: On entering audience he first set forth the essentials of discipline, using hunting as analogy: "The censor's duty lies in striking at wickedness, like the hawk soaring; when seizing prey, the weak are easily obtained, but the strong require borrowing human force."
translations.idiomatic: On his audience he first explained the essentials of discipline, comparing censors to hunting hawks: "Our duty is to strike at wrongdoing. Small prey is easily taken; powerful quarry requires the emperor's backing."

sentences.zh: 不然，不惟失其前禽，仍或有傷鷹之患矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise, not only does one lose the prey before one, but there may still be the harm of injuring the hawk."
translations.idiomatic: Without it one not only loses the quarry but may wound the hawk itself."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉其言，既出，台臣皆以為賀，風紀大振。

translations.literal: " The Emperor praised his words; when he came out, all censorate officials took it as congratulation, and disciplinary standards were greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his words; when he left, the censorate celebrated, and discipline was greatly strengthened.

sentences.zh: 又上疏陳七事，曰惜名爵、抑浮費、止括田、久任使、論好事、獎農務本、勵學養士，詔中書省舉行之。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial setting forth seven matters: cherish titles and ranks, restrain extravagant expenditures, stop land surveys for confiscation, long tenure for envoys, discuss beneficial undertakings, reward agriculture and honor the root, encourage learning and nurture scholars—an edict ordered the Central Secretariat to carry them out.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized seven reforms: cherish titles, curb extravagance, halt land confiscation surveys, lengthen official tenures, scrutinize pet projects, reward agriculture, and encourage learning. The emperor ordered the Central Secretariat to implement them.

sentences.zh: 尋俾均逸於外，拜河南行省平章政事。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted equal repose in the outer provinces and appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was eased into retirement in the provinces as pacification commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 時河南王卜憐吉歹為丞相，待以師禮，由是政化大行。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Henan Bolinjidai was chief minister and treated him with master's rites; thereby governmental transformation was greatly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Henan, Bolinjidai, was chief minister and treated him as a teacher; under their joint leadership governance flourished.

sentences.zh: 皇慶二年卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangqing he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Huangqing (1313) at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿大夫、中書平章政事、柱國，追封冀國公，諡文定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Blessings, Pacification Commissioner of the Central Secretariat, and Pillar of the State; enfeoffed as Duke of Ji, with posthumous title Wending.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he received grand master of splendid blessings, pacification commissioner of the Central Secretariat, and pillar of the state; was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with the posthumous title Wending (Cultured and Settled).

sentences.zh: 天挺嘗修《雲南實錄》五卷，又注唐人《鼓吹集》一十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: Tianting once compiled five scrolls of Veritable Records of Yunnan, and also annotated the Tang man's Drum-and-Pipe Collection in ten scrolls, both circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Tianting compiled five scrolls of Veritable Records of Yunnan and annotated the Tang Drum-and-Pipe Collection in ten scrolls, both of which circulated.

sentences.zh: 子佑，字君輔，小字朵魯別台。

translations.literal: His son You, styled Junfu, pet name Dorben Tai.
translations.idiomatic: His son You, whose style was Junfu and pet name Dorben Tai.

sentences.zh: 由宿衛補官，仁宗時拜殿中侍御史，以廉直著名，大受知遇。

translations.literal: From palace guard he filled an official post; in Renzong's time he was appointed Attending Censor in the Palace, famous for integrity and uprightness, and greatly received favor.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a palace guard, he became attending censor in the palace under Renzong, renowned for integrity, and won the emperor's strong favor.

sentences.zh: 遷陝西行省參知政事，拜陝西行御史臺侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Associate Administrator of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and appointed Attending Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to associate administrator of the Shaanxi branch secretariat and attending censor of the Shaanxi censorate.

sentences.zh: 張孔孫

translations.literal: Zhang Kongsun
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kongsun

sentences.zh: 張孔孫，字夢符，其先出遼之烏若部，為金人所並，遂遷隆安。

translations.literal: Zhang Kongsun, styled Mengfu; his ancestors came from the Wunuo tribe of Liao, were absorbed by the Jin people, and therefore moved to Long'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kongsun, whose style was Mengfu, was descended from the Wunuo tribe of Liao; absorbed by the Jin, the family moved to Long'an.

sentences.zh: 父之純，為東平萬戶府參議，夜夢謁孔子廟，得賜嘉果，已而孔孫生，因丐名於衍聖公，遂名今名。

translations.literal: His father Zhichun was Counselor of the Dongping Ten-Thousand-Household Office; at night he dreamed of visiting the Confucius temple and receiving bestowal of fine fruit; shortly after Kongsun was born, and therefore begged a name from the Duke Who Extends Sageliness, and so received his present name.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhichun was counselor of the Dongping ten-thousand-household office. He dreamed of visiting the Confucius temple and receiving fine fruit as a gift; when Kongsun was born soon after, he asked the Duke Who Extends Sageliness for a name, and received the name Kongsun.

sentences.zh: 既長，以文學名，辟萬戶府議事官，萬戶嚴忠範之兄為陝西行省平章政事，聘孔孫，以母老不應。

translations.literal: When grown he was famed for literary learning and was recruited as Deliberation Officer of the Ten-Thousand-Household Office; the elder brother of Ten-Thousand-Household Yan Zhongfan was Pacification Commissioner of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and engaged Kongsun, but because his mother was aged he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he was known for literary talent and was recruited as deliberation officer of the ten-thousand-household office. Yan Zhongfan's elder brother, pacification commissioner of Shaanxi, invited him to serve, but he declined because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 時汴梁既下，太常樂師流寓東平，舊章缺落，止存登歌一章而已。

translations.literal: At the time Bianliang had already fallen; Imperial Ancestral Temple music masters were scattered and lodged at Dongping; old regulations were missing and fallen away, and only the Ascension Hymn chapter remained.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Bianliang, imperial music masters had taken refuge in Dongping; most ritual regulations were lost, and only the Ascension Hymn survived.

sentences.zh: 世祖居潛邸，嘗召樂師至日月山觀之，至是，徐世隆奏帝，宜增設宮縣及文、武二舞，以備大典。

translations.literal: When Shizu resided at the hidden residence he once summoned music masters to Sun-Moon Mountain to observe them; at this time Xu Shilong memorialized the Emperor that palace bells and chimes and the civil and military two dances should be added to complete the great ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: While still in his princely establishment Shizu had summoned the musicians to Sun-Moon Mountain to review them. Now Xu Shilong memorialized that palace bells and chimes and the civil and military dances should be restored for the great ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 因詔徐世隆為太常卿，而孔孫以奉禮郎為之副，以董樂師，肄成，獻之京師。

translations.literal: An edict therefore made Xu Shilong Minister of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, while Kongsun as Master of Ceremonies served as his deputy, to oversee the music masters; when practice was completed it was presented in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu appointed Xu Shilong minister of the imperial ancestral temple and Kongsun, as master of ceremonies, his deputy to oversee the musicians. When the rites were perfected, they were presented in the capital.

sentences.zh: 廉希憲居政府，辟為掾。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian held position in the government and recruited him as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian, then in the central government, recruited him as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 及安童為相，尤禮重之，授戶部員外郎，出為南京總管府判官。

translations.literal: When Antong became chief minister he especially honored him with ritual respect, appointed him Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, and sent him out as Vice Magistrate of the Nanjing Chief Administrator's Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Antong became chief minister he treated Kongsun with special respect, appointed him vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, and sent him out as vice magistrate of the Nanjing chief administrator's office.

sentences.zh: 時方議下襄樊，朝廷急用兵，孔孫謂：「今以越境私販坐罪者，動以千數，宜開自新之條，俾得效戰贖死。

translations.literal: At the time they were debating the descent on Xiang and Fan; the court urgently needed troops; Kongsun said: "Today those convicted for cross-border private trade number in the thousands at a stroke—it is fitting to open a clause of self-renewal so they may serve in battle to redeem death."
translations.idiomatic: As the court debated the campaign against Xiangyang and Fancheng and urgently needed troops, Kongsun said, "Thousands are imprisoned for cross-border smuggling. Open a path to renewal so they may fight to redeem their lives."

sentences.zh: 」朝論采之。

translations.literal: " Court discussion adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 僉四川道提刑按察司事，尋升湖北道提刑按察副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Concurrent Commissioner of the Sichuan Circuit Surveillance Commission for Punishment and Investigation; soon he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Hubei Circuit Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He became concurrent commissioner of the Sichuan surveillance commission, then vice commissioner of the Hubei commission.

sentences.zh: 行部巴陵，有囚三百人，因怒龔乙建言興銀利，發其墳墓而燒其家，燒死者三人。

translations.literal: On circuit inspection at Baling there were three hundred prisoners who, in anger at Gong Yi's proposal to promote silver profits, opened his grave and burned his house—three died in the fire.
translations.idiomatic: On inspection at Baling he found three hundred prisoners who, enraged by Gong Yi's proposal to promote silver mining, had desecrated his grave and burned his house, killing three people.

sentences.zh: 有司以真圖財殺人坐之，孔孫原其情，減罪。

translations.literal: The responsible offices charged them with true intent to seize wealth and kill; Kongsun excused their circumstances and reduced the punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities charged them with murder motivated by greed for silver; Kongsun considered their motives and reduced the sentences.

sentences.zh: 遷浙西提刑按察副使，改同知保定路總管府事，俄拜侍御史，行御史臺事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Zhexi Surveillance Commission, changed to Associate Administrator of the Baoding Circuit Chief Administrator's Office, and soon appointed Attending Censor to conduct Censorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice commissioner of the Zhexi surveillance commission, then made associate administrator of Baoding, and soon attending censor acting for the censorate.

sentences.zh: 至元二十二年，安童復入相，言於帝曰：「阿合馬顓政十年，親故迎合者，往往驟進，據顯位；

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Zhiyuan, Antong again entered as chief minister and said to the Emperor: "Ahmad monopolized government for ten years; kin and friends who flattered him often suddenly advanced and held prominent posts;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Zhiyuan (1285), when Antong returned as chief minister, he told the emperor, "Ahmad dominated government for ten years; his kin and flatterers rose suddenly to high office;

sentences.zh: 獨劉宣、張孔孫二人，恬守故常，終始如一。

translations.literal: only Liu Xuan and Zhang Kongsun, two men, calmly kept to their old ways from beginning to end as one."
translations.idiomatic: only Liu Xuan and Zhang Kongsun remained unchanged from first to last."

sentences.zh: 」乃除宣吏部尚書，孔孫禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xuan was appointed Minister of Personnel and Kongsun Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was appointed minister of personnel and Kongsun vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 尋升孔孫禮部尚書，擢燕南提刑按察使。

translations.literal: Soon Kongsun was promoted to Minister of Rites and elevated to Commissioner of the Yannan Surveillance Commission for Punishment and Investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Kongsun was soon promoted to minister of rites and surveillance commissioner of Yannan.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，提刑按察司改肅政廉訪司，仍為使，蒞治於大名，一以所沒贓糴粟五千斛賑饑民。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the Surveillance Commission for Punishment and Investigation was changed to the Commission for Upholding Governance and Investigating Corruption; he remained commissioner, took up governance at Daming, and entirely used five thousand hu of grain bought with confiscated bribes to relieve famine victims.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year (1291) the surveillance commission was renamed the integrity commission; he remained commissioner at Daming and used five thousand hu of grain purchased with confiscated bribes to relieve famine victims.

sentences.zh: 拜僉河南江北行中書省事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Concurrent Counselor of the Henan and Jiangbei Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed concurrent counselor of the Henan and Jiangbei branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 亡何，除大名路總管，兼府尹，大興學校。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Chief Administrator of Daming Circuit, concurrently Prefect, and greatly raised schools.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made chief administrator and prefect of Daming Circuit and greatly expanded the schools.

sentences.zh: 有獻故河堤三百餘里於太后者，即上章，謂宜悉還細民，從之。

translations.literal: When someone presented more than three hundred li of old river embankments to the Empress Dowager, he at once submitted a memorial saying they should all be returned to the common people; his advice was followed.
translations.idiomatic: When someone offered more than three hundred li of old river embankments to the empress dowager, he memorialized that they should be returned to the common people, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 擢淮東道肅政廉訪司使，因讞獄鹽場，民尹執中兄弟誣伏為強盜，平反之。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Huaidong Circuit Commission for Upholding Governance and Investigating Corruption; because of a prison case at the salt works, the commoners Yin Zhizhong and his brothers had falsely confessed as bandits—he reversed the verdict.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to integrity commissioner of Huaidong, he reversed the conviction of the Yin Zhizhong brothers, commoners who had been forced to confess to banditry in a salt-field case.

sentences.zh: 召還，拜集賢大學士、中奉大夫，商議中書省事。

translations.literal: He was recalled, appointed Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and Grand Master for Court Audience, and deliberated on Central Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he became grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and grand master for court audience, and deliberated on Central Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 丞相完澤卒，孔孫與陳天祥上封事，薦和禮霍孫可為相。

translations.literal: When Chief Minister Wanze died, Kongsun and Chen Tianxiang submitted a sealed memorial recommending Heluohosun as fit to be chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When chief minister Wanze died, Kongsun and Chen Tianxiang submitted a sealed memorial recommending Heluohosun for the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 會地震，詔問弭災之道，孔孫條對八事，其略曰：蠻夷諸國，不可窮兵遠討；

translations.literal: When an earthquake occurred, an edict asked the way to quell calamity; Kongsun itemized eight matters in reply; in summary: the various barbarian states must not be pursued with exhausted armies in distant campaigns;
