translations.idiomatic: After an earthquake the emperor asked how to avert disaster; Kongsun listed eight points, in brief: do not exhaust the armies in distant campaigns against barbarian states;

sentences.zh: 濫官放譴，不可復加任用；

translations.literal: officials dismissed for abuse must not again be employed;
translations.idiomatic: dismissed corrupt officials must not be reappointed;

sentences.zh: 賞善罰惡，不可數賜赦宥；

translations.literal: in rewarding good and punishing evil, amnesties must not be repeatedly bestowed;
translations.idiomatic: reward the good and punish the wicked, but do not issue amnesties too often;

sentences.zh: 獻鬻寶貨，不可不為禁絕；

translations.literal: presenting and selling precious goods must not fail to be strictly forbidden;
translations.idiomatic: forbid the presentation and sale of precious goods;

sentences.zh: 供佛無益，不可虛費財用；

translations.literal: supplying the Buddha is without benefit—state funds must not be wasted in vain;
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist offerings bring no benefit—do not waste state funds on them;

sentences.zh: 上下豪侈，不可不從儉約；

translations.literal: above and below are extravagant and luxurious—frugality must be followed;
translations.idiomatic: extravagance above and below must give way to thrift;

sentences.zh: 官冗吏繁，不可不為裁減；

translations.literal: officials are redundant and clerks numerous—reduction must be carried out;
translations.idiomatic: the bureaucracy is bloated—cut redundant offices and clerks;

sentences.zh: 太廟神主，不可不備祭享。

translations.literal: the spirit tablets of the Imperial Ancestral Temple must not lack full sacrificial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: ensure full sacrifices at the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 帝悉嘉納之，賜鈔五千貫。

translations.literal: The Emperor fully praised and accepted all, and granted five thousand strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fully approved his advice and granted five thousand strings of paper money.

sentences.zh: 又累疏言：「凡七十致仕者，宜加一官；

translations.literal: He also repeatedly submitted memorials saying: "All who retire from office at seventy should receive one additional rank;
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly memorialized: "Officials who retire at seventy should receive one additional rank;

sentences.zh: 丁憂服闋者，宜待起復；

translations.literal: those who complete mourning should await recall to office;
translations.idiomatic: those who finish mourning should await recall rather than be rushed back;

sentences.zh: 宿衛之冒濫者，必當革；

translations.literal: those who improperly fill palace guard posts must be reformed;
translations.idiomatic: purge the abuses in the palace guard;

sentences.zh: 州郡之職，必當遴選，久任達魯花赤，宜量加遷轉；

translations.literal: prefectural and commandery posts must be carefully selected; darughachi long in one post should be given measured transfer and promotion;
translations.idiomatic: prefectural posts must be carefully chosen; long-serving darughachi should be rotated and promoted;

sentences.zh: 又宜增給官吏俸祿；

translations.literal: official salaries should also be increased;
translations.idiomatic: increase official salaries;

sentences.zh: 修建京師廟學，設國子生徒，給賜曲阜孔廟灑掃戶；

translations.literal: build temple schools in the capital, establish National Academy students, and grant households to sweep the Qufu Confucius temple;
translations.idiomatic: build temple schools in the capital, enroll Imperial Academy students, and grant households to maintain the Confucius temple at Qufu;

sentences.zh: 相位宜參用儒臣，不可專任文吏；

translations.literal: the chancellorship should employ Confucian ministers in combination and must not rely solely on clerical officials;
translations.idiomatic: the chancellorship should include Confucian ministers, not rely solely on clerical officials;

sentences.zh: 故相安童、伯顏、和禮霍孫與廉希憲等，各宜贈諡。

translations.literal: the former chief ministers Antong, Bayan, Heluohosun, and Lian Xixian and others should each be granted posthumous titles."
translations.idiomatic: former chief ministers Antong, Bayan, Heluohosun, Lian Xixian, and others should each receive posthumous titles."

sentences.zh: 」久之，請老還家，拜翰林學士承旨、資善大夫，致仕，集賢大學士如故。

translations.literal: " After long service he requested age and return home; he was appointed Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief and Grand Master for Fostering Goodness, retired from office, and remained Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies as before.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he asked to retire; he was made Hanlin expositor-in-chief and grand master for fostering goodness, retired from office, and retained his grand academician title at the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 大德十一年卒，年七十有五。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dade he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year of Dade (1307) at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 孔孫素以文學名，且善琴，工畫山水竹石，而騎射尤精。

translations.literal: Kongsun was always famed for literary learning, was also skilled at the zither, accomplished in painting landscapes, bamboo, and stone, and especially expert in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Kongsun was known for literary talent, excelled at the zither, painted landscapes, bamboo, and rocks, and was especially skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 及其立朝，讜言嘉論，有可觀者，士論服之。

translations.literal: When he stood at court, his forthright words and fine discourse had much worth seeing; scholarly opinion submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: In office his forthright counsel was notable, and men of learning respected him.
